google_news_sources.name: Google News - F-1/OPT/student visa
google_news_sources.query: F-1 visa OR OPT visa OR international student visa

google_news_sources.name: Google News - Green Card / I-140
google_news_sources.query: green card I-140 OR employment based green card

google_news_sources.name: Google News - immigration policy (general)
google_news_sources.query: H-1B OR immigration executive order OR visa fee

notes: Any source can be removed by deleting its entry, or disabled by setting 'always_include' appropriately.
'always_include': true means items from that source are kept even if they don't match one of the H-1B/F-1/I-140/PERM/Green Card keyword categories below (tagged with 'always_include_label' instead).
If a feed URL ever breaks (site redesign, etc.), the scraper logs a warning for that source and continues with the rest - it will not fail the whole run.
Feed URLs like natlawreview.com/rss.xml and reddit .json endpoints are unauthenticated public endpoints; if one stops working, just update or remove it here.

google_news_sources use Google News' public RSS search (news.google.com/rss/search) - this is how mainstream coverage (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, WSJ, NYT, etc.) shows up, since none of those outlets publish a plain immigration-topic RSS feed of their own. Their 'category' is forced onto every result from that query (set to null to rely on keyword tagging instead). Links point through a Google News redirect that lands on the original article - that's normal and still counts as a citation to the original outlet, shown via the article's real headline and source name.

Reddit sometimes rate-limits requests coming from GitHub Actions' shared IP ranges (HTTP 429). If r/immigration or r/h1b show up empty in the Action logs, that's Reddit throttling, not a bug - Google News + USCIS + Federal Register are the more reliable backbone.
